s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral visual field defects
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
No symptoms except night blindness
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle
ERG shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
ERG shows flat rod electroretinogram
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
OCT shows marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral visual field defects
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
No symptoms except night blindness
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle
ERG shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
ERG shows flat rod electroretinogram
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
OCT shows marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

raw.rationale: The patient's long history of night blindness since childhood, combined with the fundus examination findings of few yellow spots and an indistinct grayish circle, along with the electroretinogram showing flat rod electroretinogram and lower amplitudes compared to 30 years ago, are consistent with retinitis pigmentosa. The progressive nature of the disease is also supported by the decrease in ERG amplitudes over time.

rejected.label: complete congenital stationary night blindness
rejected.why: The disease is progressive, as indicated by the decrease in ERG amplitudes over time, which is not characteristic of congenital stationary night blindness

rejected.label: congenital stationary night blindness
rejected.why: Similar to complete congenital stationary night blindness, this condition is typically non-progressive, which does not match the patient's decreasing ERG amplitudes

rejected.label: retinal dystrophy
rejected.why: While retinal dystrophy is a broad term that could encompass the patient's symptoms, retinitis pigmentosa is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the combination of night blindness, fundus examination findings, and ERG results

rejected.label: nyctalopia
rejected.why: Nytalopia is a symptom of night blindness, not a specific disease diagnosis, and does not account for the other findings such as the fundus examination and ERG results
